clue.text: Officer in work unit in the main not losing heart

indicators.note: to sit in something is to be enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside another
a heart is the middle, so losing it means the central letter of a word is dropped

blocks.note: the erg is the physics unit of work
the main is an old poetic name for the open ocean
the word with its middle letter dropped

explanation.surface: An officer serving with a work unit at sea is holding his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic name for the open sea, and the erg is a physics unit of work; 'losing heart' takes the middle letter out of 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army or a police rank, so the general term fits.

clue.text: Revival to appear after switching components

indicators.note: swapping the two parts of a compound moves the back half round to the front

blocks.note: to turn up is to arrive or appear

explanation.surface: A revival is about to show itself once some parts have been swapped around.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb TURN UP has two parts; exchanging their places gives UP then TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement in fortunes or the economy, which is a kind of recovery after decline.

clue.text: Sin that sounds reducible to its core elements?

indicators.note: something that sounds like a thing is heard rather than spelt, so the spoken form counts

blocks.note: the two middle letters of the word, spoken as letter names, make the whole word

explanation.surface: A sin that might be boiled down to its essential ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip ENVY to its core and you have N and V; say those letters aloud and you have said the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the traditional seven deadly sins alongside pride, wrath, greed, lust, gluttony and sloth.

clue.text: Make smaller vessel to carry small car

indicators.note: a carrier holds its load inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a dish is a serving vessel
the Mini is the famous small British car

explanation.surface: Downsizing a ship to transport a compact car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a piece of crockery that holds the little car.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to reduce its size or amount, a straightforward synonym for shrinking it.

clue.text: Save others after overlooking final indication to proceed

indicators.note: to overlook something is to miss it out, so the closing letter is ignored

blocks.note: 'the rest' means the others; drop its last letter
a cue is a signal to begin, as for an actor

explanation.surface: Saving other people after you missed the last signal to go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Others' stands for 'the rest', and 'overlooking final' applies to that word, not to the cue that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger or harm, so the verbs are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Intimate female friend in Paris, duplicitous one

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
ami is French for friend
someone deceitful tells lies

explanation.surface: A close girlfriend in Paris turns out to be two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female friend in Paris' looks like AMIE, but female is F and the friend is AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being familiar with someone means being close and on intimate terms, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: That chap with a revolutionary desire is an Irish poet

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: the pronoun for a man
taken as written
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A man with radical political longings turns out to be a poet from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as political but it simply turns YEN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamus Heaney was a Northern Irish poet who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1995.

clue.text: Dear former lover, lost in thought

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Someone musing wistfully about a beloved old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like an endearment for the former lover, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced is a common British usage for something that costs a lot.

clue.text: America supplied desert plant

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America
to supply is to give

explanation.surface: The United States has provided a plant from arid lands.
explanation.walkthrough: A for America comes first, then GAVE in its sense of provided; 'desert plant' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaves are spiky succulents native to arid regions of the Americas, used for tequila and sisal.

clue.text: Taking off, having snatched cover from coffin? That’s dreadful

indicators.note: something snatched is grabbed and held, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: taking off someone is mimicking them
a pall is the cloth spread over a coffin

explanation.surface: Someone flees after stealing the cloth from a coffin, an awful act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests departing, but it means imitating someone. The clue is built as a twin of 13 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalling describes something shockingly bad, the same intensity as calling it terrible or dreadful.

clue.text: University Department involved in colourful college festivity

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up within it

blocks.note: gay in its older sense of bright and showy
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation, as in dept

explanation.surface: An academic department takes part in a bright celebration at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: U and D go inside GAY in its old sense of brightly coloured. 'Colourful' wants to describe the festivity; it is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaudy is a celebratory dinner or reunion for old members held at some Oxford and Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Version of end of scene not in pic, Nolan pic

indicators.note: an end is the final point, so only the closing letter is kept
a new version is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cut of a film where the final scene has been left out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a director's cut; the comma splits the wordplay from the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inception is the 2010 science-fiction film written and directed by Christopher Nolan, and pic is slang for a movie.

clue.text: Institute in Lausanne reorganised and put on a 12-month basis

indicators.note: to reorganise is to set things in a new order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Swiss institute restructures itself and moves to a yearly cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Lausanne is a Swiss city; its letters plus I for Institute are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To annualise figures is to express or calculate them over a full year, hence a twelve-month basis.

clue.text: Taking off, having snatched a number of bells? That’s tempting

indicators.note: something snatched is grabbed and held, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: taking off someone is mimicking them
a peal is a set of bells or the sound they ring

explanation.surface: Someone runs off having stolen some church bells, which is a temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin of 9 Down with the same frame: 'taking off' means imitating, not leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing is attractive or alluring, which matches being tempting.

clue.text: No indication of disapproval for immoral behaviour in other than the clergy

indicators.note: saying no to something leaves it out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: laxity is slackness in moral standards
a cross marks something as wrong

explanation.surface: No-one frowns on wicked conduct among ordinary churchgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the cross a teacher puts by a wrong answer; take it out of LAXITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary church members, as opposed to ordained priests and ministers; the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: Refill also reduced by 22 Across?

indicators.note: reducing something makes it shorter, so a letter is cut

blocks.note: 'too' means also; shortened by one letter
a pup is a young animal, which fits the answer at 22 Across

explanation.surface: A refill that's also been cut down by the answer to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: TOO loses a letter to give TO; 22 Across is YOUNGSTER, and a pup is a youngster, so it gives PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is an additional amount added to fill a glass or account again, which is a refill.

clue.text: Particular copper having bar turned over after place emptied

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, so only the outside letters remain
coming after means placed later in the order
turning something over flips it end to end

blocks.note: the first and last letters
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A fussy policeman knocked over a bar once the place had cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer but it is the metal's symbol. Particular here means distinctive, special.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar can mean belonging specially to one thing, as in 'peculiar to', which is the sense of particular.

clue.text: What may be loud colour

blocks.note: first meaning: an outcry
second meaning: a shade or tint

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud colour' reads as one phrase for a garish shade; split it, and the first part is the old word for a shouting clamour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a shade, and hue also survives in 'hue and cry', a noisy public outcry in pursuit of a criminal.

clue.text: Use film innovatively, with unknown factor, to create something with suspense?

indicators.note: doing something innovatively means arranging it in a new way

blocks.note: taken as written
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A director uses film inventively and adds a mystery ingredient to build a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspense in the definition is a pun on suspension, droplets held throughout a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulsify is to make an emulsion, in which tiny droplets of one liquid are held in suspension in another.

clue.text: Concerning start of machinations against property?

indicators.note: a start is the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: 'in re' is Latin legal shorthand meaning about
its first letter

explanation.surface: Something about the first moves of a plot directed at someone's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Both IN RE and IN REM are Latin legal phrases; the second, 'against the thing', names suits about property.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an action in rem is brought against a thing, usually property, rather than against a person.

clue.text: I agree to pack additional line for this fish

indicators.note: packing means stuffing things inside a container

blocks.note: more means extra
aye is yes
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An angler agrees to bring an extra line to catch this fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I agree' is the old yes of parliamentary votes, and 'line' contributes only its abbreviation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The moray eel is a large predatory eel of warm seas, so it is the fish in question.

clue.text: Country cottage, one with central heating, secured by US lawyer

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast inside it

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney
a means one
standard abbreviation, as in estate-agent listings

explanation.surface: An American lawyer has bought a rural cottage with central heating.
explanation.walkthrough: A district attorney is the American public prosecutor, and CH is the estate agent's shorthand for central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or second home, often a modest holiday cottage outside the city.

clue.text: Thin top erected over Aussie truck

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something upright makes its letters read upwards
in a down clue one thing over another sits above it

blocks.note: a lid is the top of a container
ute is Australian slang for a utility vehicle or pickup

explanation.surface: A flimsy cover is put up over an Australian pickup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' looks like an adjective, but here it is a verb, matching the verb dilute.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a liquid is to thin it by adding water, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: One inexperienced guy with no rest at work

indicators.note: things at work are being processed and reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice worker who never gets a break on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At work' fits the surface about a busy employee, but it signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, and the young are typically lacking in experience.

clue.text: Solver that is audible in greeting

indicators.note: something audible is heard, so the spoken form counts

blocks.note: the solver is addressed as 'you', and 'who' stands for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone solving the puzzle is heard calling hello.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords call the solver YOU; 'that is' becomes WHO as a relative pronoun, and the pair spoken aloud make the call.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoo-hoo is a cry used to attract someone's attention, a friendly hailing call.

clue.text: No country lover? Drag one into Northumberland area

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: to tow is to pull along
Northumberland is in the north-east of England
Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes the countryside is hauled off to Northumberland.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's most northerly county, in the North East region. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A townie is a town dweller, often one who has little feel for rural life, hence not a country lover.

clue.text: To relax is to overwhelm chart stuff with light classics

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
taken as written
pop music fills the charts

explanation.surface: The way to unwind is to drown out the hit parade with easy-listening classics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lollipops' was the conductor Thomas Beecham's term for short, popular orchestral encores; 'is' here is literal letters, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollipops are short, tuneful, popular orchestral pieces, the sweet treats of a concert programme.

clue.text: Lewd howl about women’s drawers at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the first letter is used
to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: hounds bay, a howling cry
standard abbreviation for women
its first letter

explanation.surface: A crude yowl about ladies' underwear, right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' reads as underwear, but only its first letter is used; W and D go inside BAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawdy humour is coarse and sexually suggestive, which is what lewd means.

clue.text: Spy, note, probing a lot of evidence of murder?

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the end is dropped
a probe pushes inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a body is proof of a killing; its last letter is lost
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A secret agent noting things down while examining the evidence of a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: BODY shortened gives BOD, and N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is Ian Fleming's fictional British secret agent, the most famous spy in fiction.

clue.text: Tense, distress continually returning - you can hear it in the voice

definitions.text: you can hear it in the voice

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: standard grammatical abbreviation
to gnaw is to worry or trouble persistently

explanation.surface: Nervous anxiety keeps coming back and shows up in how you speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for anxiety, but it is the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive nasal quality of speech or accent, a sound you notice when someone talks.

clue.text: Attack originating in part of East Anglia? One’s behind that

blocks.note: of can mean coming from, as in 'a man of Kent'
the Fens are the flat marshy region of eastern England
one has, said in the first person, is I have

explanation.surface: An assault launched from somewhere in eastern England, with someone backing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' expands to 'one has', and the setter speaking of himself makes it I'VE. East Anglia is the eastern bulge of England containing the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a planned military attack or campaign, so the noun matches.
